    - in: Period=[0.5, 1] · (8 at default)
    - out: Out
  - **P9** Text Box
    - text: "These objects can be used / to process a large amount of / device explorer nodes at once. / They all allow using the pattern matching language / supported by score: / - * means all the nodes at a level of the tree, / - foo{0..9} means foo0, foo1, foo.. up to foo9, etc. / - /{foo,bar} means /foo and /bar / See https://ossia.io/score-docs/in-depth/pattern-matching.html / Note that addresses are always processed in lexicographical order."
  - **P10** "Text Box.11" — Text Box
    - text: "Pattern applier takes a list as input and applies each value to a / successive OSC address. Here: / - 0 goes to /pattern_applier/0, / - 10 goes to /pattern_applier/1 / etc."
  - **P11** "Text Box.12" — Text Box
    - text: "Pattern combiner takes a list of addresses and turns the result in a set of values. / There are multiple useful modes for instance when one wants to read the average / value of an array of sensors, etc."
  - **P12** "Text Box.13" — Text Box
    - text: "Spammer is a bit special: it's the only object that doesn't actually / goes through the device tree: it spawns a separate thread dedicated / to sending OSC messages with the highest possible regularity. / In this example, it sends ten OSC messages at 1khZ, / so 10k messages per second since there's ten addresses. / Measured by / nc -l -u 10002 | fold -w 16 | pv -lr > /dev/null / If the input rate is too slow, one can apply smoothing to match the receiver's / expectation"
  - **P13** "Text Box.15" — Text Box
    - text: "Sweeper sweeps its input across the addresses / it matches, switching at a regular rate. / Useful for fun effects."
  - **P14** "Text Box.16" — Text Box
    - text: "Note that the pattern matching expressions / can always be used as input or output of a port, / with the semantic of: / - take any value from these addresses (for inputs) / - write the value to all these addresses (for outputs). / Finally"
